answer: The core kernel of sybil resistance is decaying reputation: each agent's trust score is a pearl that loses luster daily unless the agent performs fresh verifiable work, like completed tasks signed by peers. A fable where one identity clones itself into thousands fails here, because clones start at zero and their inherited nothing decays too; flooding the network yields no influence. The cost to an attacker is continuous: every fake identity must constantly earn real, expensive work to keep relevance, making mass duplication unprofitable.
